decisions.reason: As a very recent launch in an agricultural niche that fits the reusable-packaging portfolio, its performance is still uncertain, but a large firm with slack would usually give it more time before withdrawing it.

A foldable large container is strongly aligned with the firm's core logistics-packaging business, and its dedicated web presentation suggests commitment and results likely near or above aspiration for a new product.

A stackable plastic crate is close to the firm's established offering, so even if early sales are modest, management would likely retain it while learning because the resource redeployment gains are limited.

The rackable pallet fits the core pallet line and customer base, and although only lightly promoted so far, a large German manufacturer would typically continue it for another period unless performance clearly fell below aspirations.

The spill-retention pallet serves a specialized but valuable customer need within industrial logistics, and its own product page indicates enough strategic support to keep it on the market despite early uncertainty.

This plastic pallet innovation is tightly connected to the firm's main capabilities and was prominently presented, so behavioral-theory logic points to retention unless there is clear evidence of serious underperformance.
